prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Houston for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist for implants in Houston — the right provider depends on your specific case (single tooth vs full-arch, need for bone graft/sinus lift, medical history, budget, aesthetic goals). That said, the most qualified clinicians for implants are usually oral & maxillofacial surgeons, periodontists, or prosthodontists who focus on implants.

How to find the best provider for your case
- Look for the right specialty and training
  - Oral & maxillofacial surgeons (OMS) or periodontists commonly place implants; prosthodontists handle complex restorations.
  - Board certification and fellowship training are strong pluses (e.g., ABOMS for OMS).
- Experience and case mix
  - Ask how many implants they place yearly and whether they do your specific procedure (single implant, full-arch, All-on-4, sinus lifts, grafting).
- Technology and planning
  - CBCT 3D imaging, digital planning and guided surgery improve accuracy.
- Restorative coordination
  - Ideally the surgeon coordinates with the restorative dentist or a prosthodontist so the final crown/bridge fits well.
- Outcomes and follow-up
  - Ask about success/complication rates and long-term follow-up care.
- Reviews and before/after examples
  - Read patient reviews and ask to see cases similar to yours.
- Comfort and logistics
  - Sedation options, office infection control, financing, and clear cost estimates.

Questions to ask at a consultation
- Are you a specialist (OMS/periodontist/prosthodontist) and are you board-certified?
- How many implants have you placed? How many for cases like mine?
- Do you use CBCT and guided implant placement?
- Which implant systems do you use and why?
- Will you do the restoration or refer to a prosthodontist/my dentist?
- What are your complication rates and how do you handle failures?
- What’s the full cost (surgery, grafts, temporary and final restoration)? Any warranties?
- Can I see before/after photos and patient references?

Where to look for Houston providers
- UTHealth School of Dentistry (reputable academic clinic for complex cases/second opinions)
- American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID) and American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (AAOMS) directories
- Local reviews: Google, Healthgrades, Yelp, realself-type sites (take single reviews with caution)

If you want, I can:
- Help narrow options if you tell me your ZIP code/neighborhood and whether you have a complex case (bone loss, smoking, medical issues) or a simple single-tooth implant.
- Provide a short list of highly rated Houston implant specialists (I’ll need your permission to search current online listings).
